exact_statement: For the explicitly specified 797 Boolean cases, H-Hinf<=4I is certified by rational log intervals; Hinf<=2I fails in three tribes cases. In particular h_{2,3} has I=27/16 and Hinf=10-4log2(3)>2I. The actual 514-bit Boolean F=(1+z)/2+(1-z)y product(j=1..32)h_{2,8}(x_j)/2 has I=2315/128, Hinf=2 and H-Hinf-4I>1.631488620635. These refute only helper constants 2 and 4, not universal finiteness or FEI. The largest certified Hinf/I in the specified primary family is (512/1029)(22-2log2(353))>2.524150672274, at h_{3,4}.
hypotheses: Uniform independent cube inputs; Boolean outputs +-1, except explicitly labelled normalized non-Boolean controls; logarithms base two.
proof_dependencies: Elementary Fourier factorization, Parseval and physical boundary identities; threshold_paper_38pp §8.4 Proposition 8.9 as contextual exact identity, explicitly rederived.
refutes: Proposed Hinf<=2I on all Boolean functions

exact_statement: For every even n quadratic bent sign, every nonzero signed Fourier autocorrelation is zero and every unsigned autocorrelation is one; its total unsigned cost is 2^n-1, and I=n/2, so total unsigned cost cannot be universally paid by KI. Separately, sup_boolean (H-Hinf)/I = sup_boolean H/I (extended real values): for arbitrary Boolean h and integer t>=1 the balanced-core selector F built from y*h^tensor(t) satisfies H(F)-Hinf(F)=tH(h)/2 and I(F)=1+tI(h)/2. Normalized dyadic non-Boolean phi_t=3/4+(1/(4*2^t))sum(i=1..7*4^t)x_i has gap/I=2t+log2(9) and violates the singleton signed Booleanity identity; flat psi_n has Hinf/I=log2(n) but gap zero.
